Here’s each song with a short **why it’s easy** — mainly **lyrics to memorize**, with a note when guitar/tempo also helps.

### Modern Tagalog praise

1. **Salamat, Salamat** — Malayang Pilipino  
   Chorus is almost one line: *Salamat salamat O Hesus…* You learn the hook once and ride it.

2. **Aleluya Purihin Ka** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   “Aleluya” + short praise phrases. Lots of repetition, little new text per section.

3. **Purihin Pangalan Niya** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   Title *is* the chorus. Name-praise songs stick because the same words keep coming back.

4. **Papuri Kay Yahweh** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   Short call of praise to a name. Not a story song — few unique lines to hold.

5. **Isisigaw, Hallelujah** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   Built for shouting the same declaration. Memory load is low; energy does the work.

6. **Maghari** — Victory Worship  
   Chorus hangs on *maghari Ka*. Once that lands, the rest is support, not a second song.

7. **’di Magbabago** — Victory Worship  
   Title phrase is the sticky center. Fast song, but the words don’t wander.

8. **Labis Na Galak** — Faithmusic Manila  
   Joy/praise language, short sections, familiar Faithmusic shape (verse → big simple chorus).

9. **Kahanga-Hanga** — Faithmusic Manila  
   One big idea in the title. Chorus repeats the claim more than it teaches new lines.

10. **Sabik Sa Presensya Mo** — Faithmusic Manila  
    One clear desire (“I long for Your presence”). Predictable structure; chorus carries the set.

11. **Ang Lahat ay Magsasaya** — Malayang Pilipino  
    Invitation chorus (*ang lahat ay magsasaya…*). Congregation lines are short and parallel.

12. **Hari Ng Kaluwalhatian** — Faithmusic Manila  
    King/glory theme with a strong title hook. More words than #1–5, still chorus-led.

13. **Ikaw Lang** — Faithmusic Manila  
    “Only You” as the spine. Easy idea; a bit more verse text than the shout songs.

14. **Minahal** — Malayang Pilipino  
    Love song to God with a clear emotional hook. Memorability is good; verses are longer.

15. **Awit Ng Kagalakan** — Hope Filipino Worship  
    Joy theme is clear, but sections have more distinct lines than the pure title-loop songs.

16. **Dakila Ka** — Hope Filipino Worship  
    Great chorus, but more unique verse/bridge language to lock in.

17. **Pupurihin Ka** — Victory Worship  
    Modern Victory writing: singable, still more lines than Faithmusic/Hope shout tracks.

18. **Pagbabalik** — Victory Worship  
    Story/return theme. You’re memorizing a narrative, not just a slogan.

19. **Malaya Na** — Victory Worship  
    Freedom theme is clear; lyric density sits higher than early list items.

20. **Kataas-Taasan** — Victory Worship  
    Higher, denser praise language. Hardest on this list to keep word-perfect without a chart.

---

### Modern Tagalog worship

1. **Ikaw Lamang** — Faithmusic Manila  
   Title repeats; verses are short and say the same thing two ways. Classic beginner memorize.

2. **Diyos Ka Sa Amin** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   Chorus is basically one sentence: *Sa lahat ng panahon, Diyos Ka sa amin.* Guitar can be hard; words are not.

3. **Walang Katulad** — Victory Worship  
   *Walang katulad* comes back again and again. Slow tempo helps you learn while leading.

4. **Tanging Ikaw** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   “Tanging Ikaw…” opens the chorus twice. Parallel lines = less to invent from memory.

5. **Di Nagkukulang** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   Title claim is the song. You’re remembering one promise, not a paragraph.

6. **Karapat-Dapat** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   Same pattern: worthiness phrase as the spine. Short worship vocabulary.

7. **Walang Hanggan** — Malayang Pilipino  
   *Walang hanggan* is easy to hang onto; chorus stays in that lane.

8. **Ligtas** — Victory Worship  
   One word carries the idea (“safe”). Mid-slow; melody and lyric move together.

9. **Higit Pa** — Hope Filipino Worship  
   Short comparative hook (“more than…”). Not as tiny as #1–4, still chorus-first.

10. **Dakila at Tapat** — Malayang Pilipino  
    Two attributes in the title. Clear, but more full sentences than the micro-choruses.

11. **Ang Makilala Ka** — Malayang Pilipino  
    One desire (“to know You”). Memorable idea; verses add more unique wording.

12. **Pangako** — Hope Filipino Worship  
    Promise theme is simple; some sections stretch beyond a single repeating line.

13. **Natagpuan** — Hope Filipino Worship  
    “Found” story is emotional and sticky, but more poetic than slogan-worship.

14. **Tahanan** — Victory Worship  
    Home/refuge image is strong; modern Victory verses still ask for more memory work.

15. **Dakilang Pag-ibig** — Victory Worship  
    Love theme is familiar; lyric lines are longer and less copy-paste.

16. **Magtitiwala** — Hope Filipino Worship  
    Trust language is clear; structure has more distinct verse content.

17. **Ang Kalooban Mo** — Victory Worship  
    “Your will” is one idea, but the writing is denser and less loop-based.

18. **Pag-Ibig Na Kay Ganda** — Victory Worship  
    Beautiful, poetic. Harder to memorize because lines aren’t interchangeable.

19. **Kublihan** — Hope Filipino Worship  
    Shelter imagery; fewer “say the title three times” shortcuts.

20. **Pag Natapos Na** — Malayang Pilipino  
    Story/emotional arc. Most unique lines on this list — easiest to feel, hardest to memorize cold.

---

**Pattern:** easiest songs = **title or one sentence as the chorus**, few story verses, slow or mid tempo. Hardest = **story, poetry, or dense praise language**.

### 20 English praise (easiest lyrics → harder)

1. **Lord I Lift Your Name on High** — Rick Founds  
   Tiny song. One verse shape, one chorus. Almost impossible to forget.

2. **Awesome God** — Rich Mullins  
   Chorus is three words on loop. Verses are short and familiar.

3. **Open the Eyes of My Heart** — Paul Baloche  
   Same prayer repeated. Soft praise; almost no unique lines.

4. **Trading My Sorrows** — Darrell Evans  
   *Yes Lord, yes Lord…* plus a short trade list. Body memory does half the work.

5. **This is the Day** — traditional / common chorus  
   Psalm-line chorus everyone already knows from childhood church.

6. **Days of Elijah** — Robin Mark  
   Long-ish, but the chorus (*There’s no God like Jehovah*) is pure repetition.

7. **How Great is Our God** — Chris Tomlin  
   Name + “how great” loop. PH churches have sung this for years.

8. **Our God** — Chris Tomlin  
   Short power lines (*Our God is greater…*). Easy shout English.

9. **Forever** — Chris Tomlin  
   *Give thanks to the Lord…* / *Forever God is faithful…* Parallel and sticky.

10. **Blessed Be Your Name** — Matt Redman  
    Title phrase returns in every situation. Pattern makes it easy.

11. **Happy Day** — Tim Hughes  
    Clear cross/resurrection chorus. More verse words than #1–5.

12. **House of the Lord** — Phil Wickham  
    Modern, but chorus is a simple party declaration.

13. **Praise** — Elevation Worship  
    Built to chant *praise*. Lyric load stays low on purpose.

14. **This is Amazing Grace** — Phil Wickham  
    Strong chorus; verses have more unique lines.

15. **Raise a Hallelujah** — Bethel Music  
    Easy chorus; bridge adds more to hold.

16. **Way Maker** *(praise energy sets)* — Sinach  
    Already huge in PH. *Way maker, miracle worker…* is a list you can recite.

17. **Good Good Father** *(uptempo sets)* — Chris Tomlin / Housefires  
    Title chorus is easy; verses are a bit more story-shaped.

18. **Who You Say I Am** — Hillsong Worship  
    Identity chorus sticks; bridge (*I am who You say I am*) helps.

19. **Graves Into Gardens** — Elevation Worship  
    Strong hooks, more sections than the early list.

20. **Praise You Anywhere** — Brandon Lake  
    Modern and singable; denser than the classic micro-choruses.

---

### 20 English worship (easiest lyrics → harder)

1. **I Love You Lord** — Laurie Klein  
   Barely a page of lyrics. Soft, slow, unforgettable.

2. **Give Thanks** — Henry Smith  
   *Give thanks with a grateful heart…* One idea the whole way.

3. **As the Deer** — Martin Nystrom  
   Psalm 42 in simple English. Filipino rooms already know it.

4. **The Blessing** — Elevation / Kari Jobe / Cody Carnes  
   Numbers 6 on loop. Almost no new words after the first minute.

5. **Way Maker** — Sinach  
   Same list-chorus that PH congregations belt without slides.

6. **10,000 Reasons (Bless the Lord)** — Matt Redman  
   *Bless the Lord, O my soul…* Verses change; chorus never does.

7. **Here I Am to Worship** — Tim Hughes  
   Title + *You’re altogether lovely…* Short, prayerful English.

8. **Lord I Need You** — Matt Maher  
   Need/holy language, very plain. Easy for second-language singers.

9. **Goodness of God** — Bethel Music  
   *All my life You have been faithful…* Story verses, but chorus is simple.

10. **Great Are You Lord** — All Sons & Daughters  
    *It’s Your breath in our lungs…* Few lines, big room sound.

11. **Build My Life** — Housefires / Pat Barrett  
    *Holy… / I will build my life upon Your love…* Clear and repeatable.

12. **Holy Forever** — Chris Tomlin / Jenn Johnson  
    *Holy forever* does the heavy lifting.

13. **Jireh** — Elevation Worship & Maverick City  
    Name + *You are enough*. Modern PH favorite; still chorus-led.

14. **Reckless Love** — Cory Asbury  
    Easy chorus; verses/bridge add more memory work.

15. **Good Good Father** — Housefires / Chris Tomlin  
    Same title loop; intimate tempo helps first-timers.

16. **What a Beautiful Name** — Hillsong Worship  
    Beautiful chorus; more unique verse language.

17. **Firm Foundation (He Won’t)** — Cody Carnes  
    Promise chorus is simple; modern structure has more parts.

18. **Oceans (Where Feet May Fail)** — Hillsong United  
    Everyone wants it; long form and bridge make it harder cold.

19. **Waiting** / denser Bethel ballads *(e.g. overlapping “I will trust” songs)* — skip if leading alone  
    Swap for **Nothing Else** — Cody Carnes if you need a #19: one desire, still more lines than #1–8.

20. **So Will I (100 Billion X)** — Hillsong United  
    Gorgeous, wordy. Hardest memorize on this list for a Filipino room without lyrics up.

Better #19: **Nothing Else** — Cody Carnes — *I'm caught up in Your presence…* One longing, medium length.

---

### Why these work for Filipino communities

- **Plain English** — short words, few idioms  
- **Chorus-first songs** — room can sing even if verses blur  
- **Already in PH muscle memory** — Tomlin, Hillsong, Sinach, old choruses  
- **Capo-friendly** — most sit in G/C/D/A with open chords  

**Starter Sunday (English):**  
Praise: #1, #2, #7, #10 · Worship: #1, #4, #5, #6, #8

Want the blog draft as these two annotated English lists next?

### 20 English praise (very easy → still easy)

   One Psalm line. Kids and lolas sing it cold.

3. **Awesome God** — Rich Mullins  
   Chorus is three words. Low demand on range.

4. **Open the Eyes of My Heart** — Paul Baloche  
   Soft, stepwise, same prayer over and over.

5. **He Has Made Me Glad (I Will Enter His Gates)** — Leona Von Brethorst  
   Short Bible-line chorus. Almost no verse load.

6. **Trading My Sorrows** — Darrell Evans  
   *Yes Lord* loop. Easy rhythm for a room.

7. **Lord Reign in Me** — Brenton Brown  
   Simple ask, mid tempo, friendly range.

8. **Come, Now is the Time to Worship** — Brian Doerksen  
   Invitation song. Slow enough to breathe between lines.

9. **Shine, Jesus, Shine** — Graham Kendrick  
   Classic missions/praise chorus. PH churches already own it.

10. **How Great is Our God** — Chris Tomlin  
    Name + short chorus. Capo down if the room sits low.

11. **Our God** — Chris Tomlin  
    Punchy, short English. Easy shout without high acrobatics.

12. **Forever** — Chris Tomlin  
    Parallel thank-you lines. Congregation locks the chorus fast.

13. **Blessed Be Your Name** — Matt Redman  
    Same phrase in every season. Predictable and singable.

14. **Happy Day** — Tim Hughes  
    Clear story, catchy chorus, still mostly stepwise.

15. **Days of Elijah** — Robin Mark  
    Chorus repeats *no God like Jehovah*. Longer song, easy hook.

16. **Today is the Day** — Lincoln Brewster  
    Upbeat but lyrically light. Keep the key low.

17. **I Could Sing of Your Love Forever** — Delirious?  
    One sentence of love on loop. Soft praise that fills a room.

18. **We Want to See Jesus Lifted High** — Doug Horley  
    Kids/youth energy, very plain English.

19. **Mighty to Save** — Hillsong Worship  
    PH staple. Chorus is easy; don’t start in a high key.

20. **Shout to the Lord** — Hillsong Worship  
    Everyone knows it. Easiest if you drop the key a bit for the climb.

### 20 English worship (very easy → still easy)

1. **I Love You Lord** — Laurie Klein  
   Fewest words on the list. Soft and low.

2. **Give Thanks** — Henry Smith  
   One grateful idea. No surprises.

3. **God is So Good** — traditional  
   Three-word praise. Anyone can enter on the first pass.

4. **As the Deer** — Martin Nystrom  
   Gentle Psalm melody. Already in Filipino church memory.

5. **Lord, Prepare Me (Sanctuary)** — John Thompson / Randy Scruggs  
   Short dedication chorus. Easy blend for a room.

6. **Create in Me a Clean Heart** — Keith Green (common chorus form)  
   Psalm prayer in plain English. Small range.

7. **He is Lord** — traditional chorus  
   Tiny confession song. Good closer or transition.

8. **Turn Your Eyes Upon Jesus** — Helen Howarth Lemmel  
   Hymn most Filipino churches already know. Sing the refrain twice.

9. **Amazing Grace** — John Newton  
   Muscle memory. Keep it slow and low.

10. **How Great Thou Art** — Stuart K. Hine  
    Big hymn, still easy if you don’t push the high notes.

11. **Here I Am to Worship** — Tim Hughes  
    Soft modern classic. Title does the memorizing.

12. **The Heart of Worship** — Matt Redman  
    Plain repentance language. Mid-slow, friendly.

13. **Lord I Need You** — Matt Maher  
    Very plain English. Good for second-language singers.

14. **10,000 Reasons (Bless the Lord)** — Matt Redman  
    Chorus never changes. Verses are optional for a shaky lead.

15. **Way Maker** — Sinach  
    Huge in PH. List-chorus (*way maker, miracle worker…*) is easy to keep.

16. **Good Good Father** — Housefires / Chris Tomlin  
    Title loop. Not Bethel/Elevation. Keep the key comfortable.

17. **Great Are You Lord** — All Sons & Daughters  
    Few lines, big sustained notes. Easy if you don’t oversing.

18. **Build My Life** — Housefires / Pat Barrett  
    *Holy* + one building line. Clear and repeatable.

19. **Cornerstone** — Hillsong Worship  
    Hymn melody underneath. Room can lean on *My hope is built…*

20. **What a Beautiful Name** — Hillsong Worship  
    Still easy for PH rooms; a little more unique verse text than #1–12.
